sections.title: Executive verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. KRM has a fast-growing Ayurvedic hospital-services business, but weak cash conversion, earmarked IPO proceeds and unresolved revenue-policy/cash disclosures prevent a funded investment conclusion. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS rather than invented neutral scores. At ₹246.60 the modeled base return is 13.28% only if the assumed cash path is achieved, below the 15% hurdle; all ordinary returns and entry prices remain null. This is an execution-and-cash-conversion watchlist thesis, not a demonstrated compounder or an endorsement of treatment efficacy.

The strongest positive is the FY26 service revenue doubling and verified additional facilities. The decisive risk is that growth in institutional/insurance receivables, inventory and tax assets consumes earnings while restricted IPO deposits look superficially like abundant free cash. A corrected revenue-recognition policy, reconciled source anomalies, demonstrated collections and a current funded obligations bridge would change the research classification; a lower quote alone cannot cure these evidence gaps.

All factor scores are integer 1–10 or NS. BQS formula is 20% GOV +20% MOAT +12% REV +10% DUR +12% CAP +10% CASH +8% BAL +8% EXEC. GQS is 40% REV +20% DUR +15% EARN +15% CAP +10% CASH. The CASH≤3 rule caps a future fully evidenced GQS at 5; it does not replace missing CAP. BQS is NS, so IAS quality input is NS, not a rounded partial BQS. sections.title: Business overview
sections.text:
KRM earns money through Ayurvedic healthcare services, including inpatient care, consultations and associated treatment, and through Ayurvedic product sales. Its FY26 mix is 53.77% services and 46.23% products. Services contributed ₹54.6805 crore against ₹27.3197 crore a year earlier; products declined from ₹49.2330 crore to ₹47.0102 crore. Therefore growth cannot be described simply as rising medicine volumes. Patient demand, hospital occupancy, realized daily billing, clinical staffing and payer collection determine service economics; advertising, conversion, product margin and fulfillment matter for products.

Hospital revenue can be cash-paid or routed through institutional/insurance arrangements. Empanelment may broaden access but delays collection and raises receivables and administrative costs. Insurer empanelment is not a government guarantee of timely payment or clinical effectiveness. The business also uses teleconsultation and an issuer-owned e-commerce storefront; a live shop proves availability, not historical sales, repeat cohorts or product efficacy.

Manufacturing, licensed practices, staffing and location-specific approvals matter. These operating permissions must be distinguished from research evidence of outcomes. No independent controlled clinical outcome dataset or reproducible cure rate was verified; marketing descriptions are not investment facts. Forecasts value a healthcare delivery/product business, not a medical claim.

sections.title: Moat and industry position
sections.text:
A credible advantage would require demonstrably lower patient acquisition cost, trusted referrals, durable payer access, clinician retention, better collection-adjusted unit margins or proprietary validated products. KRM shows a growing service network and some accredited processes, but not enough evidence to score a deep moat. Brand royalty and promoter-linked premises also make part of the operating franchise dependent on related-party contracts rather than fully owned company IP.

The official Jaipur NABH certificate AH-2025-0362 covers Panchakarma, 13 May 2025–12 May 2028. It is not a blanket endorsement of all sites, future renewals or cures. Delhi renewal was pending in the prospectus; a current renewal certificate was not verified. Location-specific issuer announcements are retained as company statements. Patient litigation allegations remain allegations, not adjudicated clinical conclusions.

| Peer | FY26 standalone revenue | PAT | CFO | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jeena Sikho | 801.3464 | 222.1757 | 261.9925 | Larger delivery network; Ind AS lease basis differs. |
| Sat Kartar Life | 193.8386 | 17.2586 | 0.1439 | D2C-heavy mix; debt-in-CFO adjusted cash 3.2906. |
| Dabur | 13,192.6 | Not used | Not used | Diversified FMCG scale, not a direct hospital valuation peer. |

All monetary peer values are ₹ crore. These contrasts support competition and cash discipline, not a mechanically transferable multiple. No synchronized peer market-price dataset was used. Accreditation and advertising cannot earn a monopoly or medical-efficacy premium.

sections.text:

| 2026 | 101.69 | 25.14 | 32.84% |

The selected FY23–FY26 window spans three intervals and yields 4.43%; starting REV2, net+1 for two completed annual recovery periods with Q1 corroboration, final REV3. Five- and ten-year CAGRs are unavailable, not 0. FY22 revenue was verified from the original financial statement rather than substituting total income ₹40.9511 crore. Its four-year CAGR 25.53% and FY24–26 trough-base CAGR 23.05% are context only, not cherry-picked scoring windows.

FY24 revenue fell 24.79%; management attributes strategic resource reallocation toward hospitals, which explains intent but does not erase the lost sales. FY25 and FY26 grew 14.0% and 32.84%. Q1 FY27 grew 31.04%, PAT 124.15%, with service revenue ₹23.922 crore. TTM revenue ₹109.3469 crore and PAT ₹25.1517 crore use FY26 +current Q1− prior Q1, not annualization. Prior Q1 figures were not reviewed; no TTM cash-flow statement is available. Price/volume/patient cohort separation is ND. Acquisition of a previously nil-turnover subsidiary is not counted as organic growth evidence.

sections.title: Growth quality and reinvestment runway
sections.text:
The runway is bounded by clinician supply, permitted facilities, patient acquisition, payer access, bed occupancy and collectible billing rather than a broad Ayurveda market-size estimate. The May call's 223 beds× 69% occupancy× ₹8,400 ARPPD× 365 implies ₹47.18 crore inpatient billing, compared with FY26 services ₹54.68 crore. Outpatient/other services could explain the remainder, but bed averaging and timing are not audited; this is a consistency diagnostic, not a reconciled patient-volume record.

The base model grows average modeled beds 326/390/460/530/600/660 for FY27–32, occupancy 68% to 70%, ARPPD ₹8,500 to ₹9,500, other service income ₹15 to ₹30 crore and products ₹45 to ₹60 crore. The bull scales to 1,050 average beds at 74%; the bear reaches 380 at 55%. These are analyst scenarios, deliberately below management's 1, 500–2,000 beds in three years aspiration. Average modeled beds are not announced end-period capacity.

Annual capital needs include ordinary capex 4% of sales base, separate remaining IPO project capex ₹15.09 crore, incremental operating WC, tax-credit absorption 2% of revenue and incremental security deposits linked to service scale. HR-funded operating costs remain in EBITDA; releasing earmarked funds is a financing source, not extra profit. CAP is NS because no facility cohort contains attributable invested capital, fully loaded losses, mature margins and cash collections. A current book ROCE proxy cannot repair that gap. GQS remains NS with a binding conditional ceiling 5 for persistently weak cash.

sections.title: Management governance and execution
sections.text:
Promoter group holds 69.30%, with no pledged shares reported in September. FY26 related-party sales ₹26.0304 crore are 25.60% of revenue. Related rent ₹1.8231 crore plus royalty ₹1.25 crore equals 15.27% of PAT. These are disclosed arrangements and audited compliance is counterevidence to abuse; nevertheless concentration, transfer pricing and company ownership of the economic franchise deserve scrutiny. FY25 royalty P&L ₹1.00 crore and related-party note ₹1.18 crore differ, potentially tax presentation but not independently reconciled. No allegation of diversion is made.

| Date or target | Observed evidence | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| May 2026 | 223 beds; 500 FY27 and 1, 500–2,000 three-year aspirations | Management targets, not sanctioned funded capacity. |
| 16 June | 23 bed MSS Hospital opened | Verified issuer disclosure supports delivery. |
| 30 June | Telemedicine/CRM capex 0; HR use 0.05 | Roll-forward permitted, but execution not completed. |
| 9 July | Gurugram 60–100 beds proposed; ₹0.15 crore setup quoted | Scope vs May ₹2.5–3 lakh/bed not reconciled; not full unit economics. |
| 10 August | 103 beds added YTD per presentation | Issuer claim, not audited average utilization. |
| 23 September | Ghaziabad day-care opened, 9-year lease | October 6 filing before cutoff verifies announcement. |
| 30 September | AGM approved ₹0.20 crore issue-cost/GCP variation | Not proof earlier WC timing approval submitted. |

CARE reports no object deviation yet flags ₹10.91 crore early working-capital deployment against original timing without requisite timing approvals submitted. September approval resolved the separate cost/GCP variation. Company answered NSE clarification on 24 July with additional H2 balancing-note/audit submissions and corrected certificates; no verified exchange closure, but not an unanswered query. CFO resignation effective 6 September states personal reasons/no other material reason; replacement effective 7 September is disclosed. Internal-auditor appointment 28 March is not evidence an audit occurred.

Total-asset residual ₹0.0003 crore is rounding. Prospectus F24 explains restatement through gratuity and delayed-tax interest: FY25 PAT+₹0.8831 crore, FY24−₹0.4618 crore, FY23 stated−₹0.4118 crore. Its FY23 arithmetic still fails by ₹0.0407 crore (7.9691−0.4118=7.5573, not 7.5980), as does equity after disclosed adjustments. Prospectus F7 cash closing ₹0.7538 crore versus components ₹0.2300 crore leaves ₹0.5238 crore unexplained. Original FY23 cash data corroborate ending ₹0.2299 crore. The errors are limited, identified discrepancies, not a claim all restatement is unexplained.

FY26 issue cash net ₹70.69 crore reconciles to IPO ₹77.49+placement ₹4.01016−reserve-netted cost ₹10.8988+IPO interest ₹0.0906=₹70.69196 crore. Monitoring gross expense ₹11.77 differs from reserve deduction by ₹0.8712 crore; tax netting/timing unverified. The IPO cash bridge separately moves ₹3.86 crore positive OD from apparent free cash into earmarked proceeds. March free cash ₹5.6528 crore excludes this earmark; ₹34.31 crore separate IPO pool, ₹7.81 crore security FD and ₹0.157 crore CSR lien are never double counted. June remaining ₹30.16 crore versus FD principal ₹30.19 crore includes reinvested interest, not missing cash. Restricted FD market value ₹30.45 crore is neither extra free cash nor principal.

Receivable days average 62.55 versus FY25 about 42.11; closing 81.57. Older-than-one-year receivables ₹2.2799 crore lack a recorded loss allowance in the reviewed table. Government balances ₹13.3549 crore and inventory ₹9.0285 crore are not spendable money. June AR and inventory increased ₹8.2206 crore/₹6.2741 crore; short debt ₹0.7198 crore reappeared. June OCA ₹45.5402 crore contains ₹15.12 crore earmarked FD, so a headline working-capital certificate is not a usable cash calculation.

Full statutory audit/CARO/IFC packages FY23–26 were inspected. Main and IFC opinions are unmodified; FY25–26 edit log all-year and no tampering reported; FY24 April 1–23 gap is historical. CARO bank-current-assets comparison is inapplicable below ₹5 crore sanctioned limits, not a positive reconciliation opinion. FY23 no-interest loan wording conflicts narrowly with no-loan clause. FY25 auditor resignation aligns with February 28, 2025 departure for preoccupation/March 5 successor; FY26 repeated wording has chronology ambiguity. FY26 no internal audit conducted, TDS ₹222660 overdue, and Note 2.8 p 128 software/IT revenue policy do not disappear under a clean main opinion. Consumer claim ₹0.505 crore remains pending in IPO disclosure, not an adjudicated liability; personal promoter cases ₹2.5 crore are excluded from company debt.

FY26 reported EPS ₹9.46 uses closing 21,260,800 shares; FY25 reported ₹747.61 uses 150,000 unadjusted shares. Current-share PAT/share is ₹9.46 FY26 and ₹5.27 FY25 statutory, not an EPS collapse. Pre IPO 15 million adjusted shares grew 41.74% to 21.2608 million, causing 29.45% holder dilution; split/bonus alone are not economic dilution. FY26 average-book capital ROCE would be distorted by late IPO cash and asset mix. Neither this proxy nor rising margin supports a CAP point.

A limited book-capital cross-check gives FY25 EBIT/average(equity+debt) of 38.92% and FY26 34.57%. The FY25 statutory equity comparative is ₹23.8953 crore, distinct from IPO-restated ₹23.8758 crore. This deliberately unadjusted proxy includes late IPO cash in the capital denominator and omits lease capitalization under AS; it is not incremental project ROIC or a CAP substitute. Historical normalized PAT proxies in the full financial table exclude other income and apply a constant 26% tax rate to operating EBITDA less depreciation and reported finance cost; they are analyst calculations, not revised audited profits. Free cash flow uses cash capex; maintenance versus growth capex is not separately disclosed.

sections.title: Valuation and market expectations
sections.text:
At ₹246.60, market cap ₹524.2913 crore, FY26 PE26.06 x, indicative TTM PE20.85 x and book multiple 4.57 x. FY26 EV/normalized EBITDA17.04 x uses only historical free cash and legacy gratuity, not asserted October EV. Operating property is not added again; leases remain rental expense under AS, without invented ROU debt. No unjustified peer premium or cure-driven valuation is applied.

| Case | Terminal TTM revenue ₹ crore | Exit EV/EBITDA | Non-rescue funded path | Conditional IRR | Peak cash gap ₹ crore |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bear | 110.46 | 8 | False | NS | 14.79 |
| base | 239.33 | 12 | True | 13.28% | 0.00 |
| bull | 395.95 | 16 | True | 35.60% | 0.00 |

All ordinary returns and ordinary entry prices are NS. Base conditional terminal algebra ₹460.07/share yields 13.28% only on assumed funding; below 15%. It is not an investable target. Terminal TTM PAT cross-check 19.18 x uses normalized 26% tax. Terminal equity=exit multiple× TTM EBITDA+closing cash−required operating cash−debt−legacy gratuity−bear claim reserve. No restricted deposit, IPO cash, tax credit, operational property or prospective property-sale surplus is added. Explicit five calendar-year endpoint 20 October 2031 uses 203/366 FY32 weight; FY32 post-terminal cash does not govern this horizon.

The dated bridge retains June actual revenue/normalized profit and operating WC checkpoints, June known IPO draws ₹4.15 crore and short debt ₹0.7198 crore, and August 5 acquisition ₹0.01 crore. Q1 capex/cash tax/guarantee timing remains an assumption, not a reconstructed actual cash statement. Residual FY27 economics follow June; model opening free cash ₹5.6528 crore is March, not October. Base June modeled cash ₹6.0151 crore and October ₹10.6965 crore are conditional. Cash floor max ₹3 crore or 5% revenue is roughly 26 days of 70%-of revenue cash cost, an analyst buffer; 8% stress breaches. IPO objects have separate nonnegative buckets; HR/GCP draws fund costs already in operations/capex rather than manufacture profit. The ₹3.5 crore property sale agreement remains excluded.

Reverse expectations verifies a financed conditional 15% crossing at 1.53% extra annual scale over base, with fixed 12 x exit multiple. The crossing preserves all cash floors; it is not an endpoint substituted for a root. It is also not ordinary return support. At 12/15/18% hurdles, conditional base entry algebra is ₹261.06, ₹228.74, ₹201.10; none is an actionable entry price until gates clear.

| Linked stress | Funded non-rescue | Conditional IRR | Peak gap ₹ crore |
|---|---|---|---|
| cash_floor_8 pct | False | NS | 2.73 |
| margin_down_5 pp | True | 8.73% | 0.00 |
| wc_up_10 pp | False | NS | 1.83 |
| cash_on_hand_not_available | False | NS | 2.97 |
| tax_credit_drag_5 pct | False | NS | 0.42 |
| capex_8 pct | False | NS | 0.75 |
| combined_squeeze | False | NS | 15.26 |

Growth× multiple grid uses−5/0/+5% extra annual scale and 8/10/12/16 x exit multiples, retaining full annual and segmented cash rows. Rescue is separate: equity@₹120, gross need=net gap/95%, 5% fees, new shares are rounded up to whole shares; gross proceeds equal whole shares × ₹120. Ownership dilution=1−old/new, not new/old−1. No finance provider/availability asserted. DCF is not used because uncertain cash classification/perimeter makes a perpetual terminal assumption less informative; terminal-value share is NA, not silently omitted.

Rescue shares are rounded up to whole units and gross proceeds, fees and net cash are recalculated. Rescue is assumed prefunded immediately before a cash-floor shortfall within a piecewise-linear period, not raised only after insolvency. This is a counterfactual availability assumption. The operating cash floor grows smoothly with the revenue checkpoint, and terminal cash uses terminal TTM revenue rather than a full post-terminal FY32 requirement. Terminal trailing earnings use exact date overlaps: 162/365 of FY31 plus 203/366 of FY32, covering 365 actual days; weights need not sum to one when a fiscal year contains a leap day.

Liquidity at the illustrative ₹5 lakh reference position:
| Window | Mean daily value ₹ crore | Median daily value ₹ crore | Days at 2% | Days at 5% | Days at 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 sessions | 2.1712 | 1.8693 | 1.337 | 0.535 | 0.267 |
| 60 sessions | 2.7591 | 2.0134 | 1.242 | 0.497 | 0.248 |
The daily-value denominator is the lower of mean and median. All 60 sessions have valid issuer rows and none has zero volume. At ₹246.60, a 1,000-share lot costs ₹246,600; two lots cost ₹493,200 and three ₹739,800. At 5% participation, median whole-lot daily capacity is 3,000 shares and two sessions round to zero capacity. At 2%, capacity is 1,000 shares and 14 sessions round to zero; at 10%, capacity is 6,000 and none rounds to zero. Top five sessions contribute 24.22% of traded value. Historical ST through 7 August changed to SM from 10 August. The latest official master reports active SM and a ₹197.30–₹295.90 band, not a current executable bid. Live spread, queues and comprehensive surveillance status remain unverified. The reference position is not a recommended allocation or promise of liquidation.

sections.title: Bear case and permanent loss path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that an entire traditional-healthcare category lacks demand. It is that payer-led hospital growth can be booked at high margin while claims take longer to collect, inventories grow and advertising/clinical costs remain cash expenses. New sites then demand security deposits and setup costs before mature occupancy. A quality-of-care or advertising dispute could reduce referrals or empanelment and raise compliance costs simultaneously. Related brand/property payments and public float constraints can amplify shareholder downside without proving management misconduct.

The bear model uses lower occupancy, product revenue and margins with 70%-of revenue early WC; its pre-entry cash becomes negative and the peak required cash shortfall is ₹14.79 crore. No non-rescue IRR or entry price is allowed after that breach. Terminal ₹95.75 per-share algebra is diagnostic only, not an available liquidation value. The separate rescue case imposes fees and dilution at ₹120; shareholders bear the reduction in claim even if operations survive. Repeated funding stress is not disguised as negative debt.

Cash-on-hand unavailability, higher cash floor, tax-credit delay and higher capex can separately breach the base path. Missing receivable recoverability and clinical outcomes prevent asset/reputation claims from providing dependable downside support. Actual audit reports do not identify lender default or material going-concern uncertainty; stress loss is an analytical scenario, not a statement the company is insolvent. Durable collection failure or verified material clinical/regulatory sanctions would break the thesis sooner than a temporary stock price fall.

sections.title: Fivefold and tenfold feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold price returns over five years require 37.97% and 58.49% annual price growth. At 15 x terminal PE, 20% PAT margin and unchanged shares, required revenue is ₹873.82 crore and ₹1747.64 crore, versus ₹101.69 crore FY26 and ₹239.33 crore conditional base terminal TTM. Dilution increases the required earnings pool.

The bull produces ₹395.95 crore terminal TTM revenue, not a validated 5× case. Management's bed target might create capacity, but utilization, billing, collections, staffing, capex and economic ownership must all follow. Large TAM, a rising quote or a speculative exit multiple cannot replace this bridge. No 5×/10× probability or guaranteed outcome is assigned. The appropriate question is whether incremental facilities generate reliable cash after fully loaded capital, not whether an aspirational bed count can be multiplied by optimistic ARPPD.

sections.title: Monitoring plan
sections.text:
| KPI | Baseline | Evidence or threshold that matters |
|---|---|---|
| Collections | FY26 closing AR 22.7272 crore; June 30.9478 crore | Recover overdue>1 year 2.2799 crore; AR days stably<70 with cash proof supports improvement;>100 or aging growth warns. |
| Cash conversion | 2-year statutory CFO/PAT 14.71% | Two disclosed half-years/full year cash conversion>70%, after-interest positive; not reclassified deposit release. |
| IPO funds | June unutilized 30.16 crore | Next CARE report separate traceability, object draws, timing approvals and current free cash. |
| Inventory and tax | June inventory 15.3026 crore; March government balances 13.3549 crore | No persistent growth faster than revenue; reconcile refund/credit use. |
| Accounting policy | FY26 p 128 software policy | Correct company-specific recognition note and cash/restatement/issue expense bridges. |
| Facilities | 223 May beds; 103 YTD added August claim | Facility-by-facility licensed opening, average beds, occupancy, ARPPD, collections, fully loaded ROIC. |
| Execution | June IPO telemedicine/CRM capex 0 | Evidence of committed contracts, actual capex and delivery within funding. |
| Governance | 25.60% RPT sales; royalty 1.25 crore | Renewals/pricing independent review; clarify claim status, CARO timing and internal audit completion. |
| Liquidity | 60 sessions complete; lot 1000 | Refresh 20/60 sessions, current lot/surveillance, spread/queues before any implementation. |

These are specific research falsification checks, not price alerts or automated trading instructions. A new funding bridge must include known subsequent events and restrictions rather than merely a management assertion that working capital is positive. A corrected disclosure can improve confidence; a target announcement alone cannot.

sections.title: Final classification and conditional action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. BQS NS, Growth Quality Score NS and IAS NS, with no ranking eligibility. G1 Conditional/G2 Hold/G3 Hold/G4 Conditional. The business is understandable and there is real reported service growth, but it has not demonstrated the cash conversion and incremental return record needed for a compounder designation. This conclusion is not an Avoid—governance judgment and does not assert fraud, diversion, default or medical inefficacy.

Priority is to reconcile the financial-policy/cash disclosures and substantiate current unrestricted funding against real commitments. After that, attributable hospital returns and sustained collections could complete CAP / BAL / R and permit a fair matrix classification. The present price gives only 13.28% conditional base IRR versus 15% hurdle; lowering price improves algebra but does not cure G2/G3. Ordinary expected return/entry price remain NS. A materially stronger collection record, properly funded execution and reliable accounting would justify reconsideration; independent clinical/regulatory facts could either strengthen or weaken the economic case. Any future action also requires fresh quote, current lot/restrictions and a user-specific position, none of which is assumed here.

sections.title: Sources assumptions and open questions
sections.text:
Sources below are original exchange/company filings, official NABH material, statutory peer reports and official NSE market data. Primary business claims are differentiated from management targets, analyst assumptions and unknowns in the evidence ledger. All statement amounts are converted from ₹ lakh to ₹ crore by÷100; shares and ₹/share remain unscaled. Cash capex means cash purchase of PPE, not PPE balance change. Debt excludes operating leases under AS; cash interest remains separate from CFO. Pre IPO split/bonus is distinct from fresh issue dilution.

Open questions: corrected healthcare-specific revenue policy; FY23 cash endpoint and F24 ₹4.07 lakh residual; gross/net IPO expense gap ₹0.8712 crore and royalty tax presentation; current free cash and timing-approval traceability; receivable ageing and tax credit realization; hospital cohort cash returns; location-specific licenses/renewals; pending consumer claim outcome; exact auditor-resignation chronology. These gaps do not convert unknowns to adverse facts. FY24 asset netting and FY25 CFO classification are resolved or near-reconciled and are not retained as open failures.

The cash buffer, occupancy, billing, margins, WC, capex, tax credit absorption, security deposits and exit multiples are explicit analyst assumptions. Model reproduction checks arithmetic and artifact consistency, not external truth or fresh authentication. Original source URLs, locators and SHA256 digests are preserved; raw PDFs, OCR, HTML, images and personal identifier lists are excluded from analytical backups. Historical web information with unverified publication timing is flagged and does not establish post-cutoff events. This financial research does not validate clinical efficacy or replace medical care.
